page.description: Linux Lite editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A lightweight Ubuntu-based desktop aimed at people moving from Windows, with Xfce and a small set of preinstalled tools. One 64-bit image.
pros: Xfce desktop that stays usable on modest hardware.
Familiar layout for people coming from Windows.
Small preinstalled set, so little has to be removed.
The project publishes a checksum for every ISO.
cons: Only a 64-bit image is published for this release.
A small team, so release cadence follows Ubuntu but support statements are sparse.
Little of the tooling is unique to Linux Lite; it is a tuned Ubuntu base.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of Linux Lite 4.2 from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 8.0 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

page.status: One path: the 64-bit ISO from the project's SourceForge, written with dd or any image writer. Writing erases the stick; the installer then partitions or erases the target disk.
